# Independent exact audit: the eleven-point Jensen graph counterexample



Index the base points by

    p0=(0,0,1), p1=(1,0,0), p2=(1,0,1), p3=(1,0,2),
    p4=(1,1,0), p5=(1,1,1), p6=(2,0,1), p7=(2,1,0),
    p8=(2,1,1), p9=(2,1,2), p10=(2,2,0).

Set P={p0,...,p10}, let g have values

    (1,1,1/2,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0),

and let W be the nine points with indices 0,1,3,4,5,6,7,8,10.

## 1. Complete lattice and minimal-face checks

The following supporting inequalities hold on all eleven points:

    x+z>=1, y<=x, -x+y+z<=1, -x+2y+z<=2,
    y>=0, z>=0, x-y-z<=1, x-y+z<=3, x<=2.

The convex hull lies in [0,2]^3. Checking all 27 integer box points against these inequalities gives exactly P. Since every listed point belongs to conv(P) by definition, this proves `conv(P) intersect Z^3=P`. Every listed point lies on a supporting plane, so the polytope is hollow.

Only p2 and p8 are nonvertices. The exact minimal faces are

    p2: y=0, with points {p0,p1,p2,p3,p6},
    p8: x=2, with points {p6,p7,p8,p9,p10}.

Indeed p2 is the average of the four corners p0,p1,p3,p6, and

    p8=p6/4+p7/8+3p9/8+p10/4,

so both lie in the relative interiors of the displayed two-dimensional faces. Every other point is exposed; the verifier checks that the sum of the active supporting normals uniquely exposes it among P.

On the y=0 face, g is exactly `(3-x-z)/2`. On the x=2 face it is identically zero. Every anchored representation at a nonvertex is confined to its minimal face; a vertex has only trivial representations. Therefore g belongs to L(P) for ALL anchored representations, not only for a selected subset.

The complete affine relation space of these faces is generated by

    p0+p6-2p2=0, p1+p3-2p2=0,
    p7+p9-2p8=0, p6+p10-p7-p8=0,

with the same zero coefficient sums. These four relations are independent, and each five-point plane has exactly two independent affine relations. Hence dim L(P)=11-4=7. The displayed height satisfies every relation exactly.

## 2. The exact base deletion kernel

The point p2 belongs to every convex hull `conv(W minus {w})`, because

    p2=(p0+p6)/2=(p1+p3)/2.

The two pairs are disjoint; deletion of one W point leaves at least one complete pair.

Each w in W is outside `conv(W minus {w})`. The following table gives an integer normal u uniquely maximized at that point, its value, and its minimum gap over the other W points:

| index | u | u dot p | minimum gap |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| 0 | (-3,1,0) | 0 | 2 |
| 1 | (0,-2,-3) | 0 | 2 |
| 3 | (0,1,3) | 6 | 2 |
| 4 | (-2,1,-2) | -1 | 1 |
| 5 | (-2,3,2) | 3 | 1 |
| 6 | (3,-2,0) | 6 | 2 |
| 7 | (2,-1,-2) | 3 | 1 |
| 8 | (2,1,2) | 7 | 1 |
| 10 | (0,2,0) | 4 | 2 |

The only remaining base point, p9, is outside conv(W), since `y+z<=2` on every W point but y+z=3 at p9. These facts prove exactly

    P intersect intersection_(w in W) conv(W minus {w})={p2}.

As a separate independent check, a rational Caratheodory enumeration of every deletion hull in R^3 reproduced this singleton kernel; repeating the membership test in the lifted R^4 graph gave an empty integral kernel. The explicit midpoint and separation certificate above makes that numerical enumeration unnecessary for the proof.

## 3. The integral graph is an actual lattice-convex set

Let q_i=(p_i,g(p_i)), and let T consist of the ten integral graph points, namely all q_i except q2. First take the hull of all eleven rational graph points. At any integer base j its source representation uses base points in P, since P is lattice-convex. Every anchored representation preserves g, so its fiber at j is the singleton (j,g(j)). Therefore the only integral points in that hull are exactly T; the base p2 carries only height 1/2.

Since T is contained in its own convex hull and that hull is contained in the eleven-point graph hull, it follows that

    conv(T) intersect Z^4=T.

This establishes the required exact arithmetic filter. It is not merely an assertion that the named graph points happen to be integral.

## 4. Nine critical convex sets and exact Helly number

For each w in W define

    C_w=conv{q_i: p_i in W minus {w}}.

Projection maps their common intersection in T into the base deletion kernel {p2}. But T has no point above p2. Hence `T intersect intersection_w C_w` is empty. If the w-indexed set is deleted, q_w belongs to every remaining set. This is an exact minimal infeasible family of nine convex sets, proving h(T)>=9.

In fact h(T)=9. Every finite ten-point set has Helly number at most ten. If a minimal infeasible family had ten members, its distinct deletion witnesses would be all of T, and the intersection of the ten convex hulls obtained by deleting one witness would have to miss T. However

    q8=(q7+q9)/2

is an integral graph midpoint. It belongs to conv(T minus {q8}) and belongs trivially to every other deletion hull. Thus no ten-member minimal infeasible family exists, and h(T)<=9.

The proof therefore yields the exact strict arithmetic-budget failure `h(T)=9>8=2^3`. All sets and separating coefficients are rational or integral; no floating-point inference is used.

Independent verifier: `supporting computation verify_eleventh_point_jensen_graph_audit.py`.

## File-specific final audit

The completed source `candidate 5c9190df7c42c598` has now been independently read in full. Its standalone verifier `supporting computation verify_integral_jensen_graph_filter_counterexample.py` also passes. The facet-polytope equality, strict interior point, alternative simpler exposing normals, full four-dimensional affine rank of the nine-vertex graph polytope, and direct integral emptiness assertion all agree with the independent certificate above. In particular the source's claimed affine basis p3,p4,p5,p6 has determinant of absolute value one, so the added nonzero-height point supplies the fourth graph direction. The exact conclusion h(T)=9 and the separation from the earlier thirteen-point special case are correct. No correction is needed.
